question.prompt: In \(\triangle ABC,\) \(AB = 10,\) \(AC = 18,\) and \(\angle B = 130^\circ.\) Let \(O\) be the center of the circle containing points \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C.\) What is the degree measure of \(\angle CAO?\)

solutions.title: Follow the intercepted arc
solutions.explanation:
The angle at \(B\) determines the arcs between \(A\) and \(C\), which will give the angle between the radii \(OA\) and \(OC\).

By the inscribed angle theorem, the arc from \(A\) to \(C\) that does not contain \(B\) measures
\[
2\cdot130^\circ=260^\circ.
\]
The remaining arc therefore measures
\[
360^\circ-260^\circ=100^\circ.
\]
This is the arc corresponding to the smaller central angle, so \(\angle AOC=100^\circ\).

Since \(OA\) and \(OC\) are radii of the same circle, \(OA=OC\). Thus triangle \(AOC\) has equal base angles, giving
\[
\angle CAO=\frac{180^\circ-100^\circ}{2}=\boxed{40^\circ}.
\]
The answer is choice C.

solutions.title: Use a diameter
solutions.explanation:
A diameter through \(A\) puts the desired angle into a right triangle. Let \(D\) be the point diametrically opposite \(A\), so \(O\) lies on segment \(AD\).

Because \(AD\) is a diameter, \(\angle ACD=90^\circ\). Consequently, \(\angle ADC\) is acute.

Inscribed angles with endpoints \(A\) and \(C\) are equal when their vertices lie on the same side of chord \(AC\). Since \(\angle ABC=130^\circ\) is obtuse while \(\angle ADC\) is acute, \(B\) and \(D\) must lie on opposite sides of \(AC\). They are therefore opposite vertices of cyclic quadrilateral \(ABCD\). Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to \(180^\circ\), so
\[
\angle ADC=180^\circ-130^\circ=50^\circ.
\]
Now the angle sum in right triangle \(ACD\) gives
\[
\angle CAD=180^\circ-90^\circ-50^\circ=40^\circ.
\]
Rays \(AO\) and \(AD\) coincide, so \(\angle CAO=\angle CAD=\boxed{40^\circ}\), choice C.
